title: Add Verify to a Moq test that only calls Setup
summary: Setup never checks that a call happened. Verify with Times.Once counts it, It.Is<T> matches a class argument that Equals cannot, and VerifyNoOtherCalls catches the extra mail.

turns.user: i commented out the confirmation mail in OrderService and this test still passes. whats the point of it

assistant.body: Great catch! Setup only says how the mock behaves when it is called. It never checks that the call happened. And new Mock<IMailer>() is MockBehavior.Loose by default, so a call with no setup returns a default value instead of throwing. Right now the test proves only that PlaceAsync does not throw. Verify is what checks a call, and Times says how many.
With Times.Once(), the test fails when the mail is forgotten and also when it is sent twice.

turns.user: put the mail back and now it fails. Expected invocation on the mock once, but was 0 times. the log says it sent

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. When you pass a plain value to Verify, Moq compares it with the real argument using Equals. Mail is an ordinary class, not a record, so Equals compares references, and the instance the test creates never matches even with the same contents. It.Is<Mail> takes a condition and compares contents instead. Pinning the exact subject makes the test brittle, so it checks only the recipient and the order number.
sed -i '' 's/new Mail("a@example.com", "Order 42 confirmed"),/It.Is<Mail>(x => x.To == "a@example.com" \&\& x.Subject.Contains("42")),/' tests/Orders.Tests/OrderServiceTests.cs

turns.user: passes. oh we once had a bug where the admin got the same confirmation too. does this catch that

assistant.body: TL;DR: not yet. Verify counts the calls that match the It.Is<Mail> condition, so a second call addressed to the admin still passes. Add VerifyNoOtherCalls at the end and the test fails if any call is left that no Verify accounted for. Note: a call that only matched a Setup does not count as verified.
